 Alex Pretti’s parents call on DOJ to release findings 9 months after their son’s death
 By KSTP 
 --> 
 A sign laid at the site where Alex Pretti was killed by Border Patrol officers says he was "killed for helping his neighbors." (KSTP)
 The parents of Alex Pretti say that the Department of Justice (DOJ) has left them in the dark in the nine months since their son was killed by federal immigration agents.
 Michael Pretti and Susan Pretti were joined by their attorney Steve Schleicher as they held their first press conference since Alex’s death on Jan. 24, 2026 during Operation Metro Surge.
 They emphasized that the DOJ has not been transparent in their findings so far.
 PREVIOUS: FBI will not share access to Alex Pretti shooting evidence with Minnesota officials, BCA says 
 Alex Pretti was a 37-year-old ICU nurse at the time of his death.
 Government records obtained by ProPublica identified the agents involved as Border Patrol agent Jesus Ochoa, 43, and Customs and Border Protection officer Raymundo Gutierrez, 35.
 At this point, no charges have been filed against the federal immigration agents who were involved.
 5 EYEWITNESS NEWS has reached out to the DOJ for a statement on the status of the investigation.
